notes: Built-in rules have logic in lib/rules.js keyed by id; their thresholds come from 'params' here. Any rule with a 'match' block and an id not handled by lib/rules.js is compiled as a custom row rule (see README).

rules.name: High 404 volume from single public client
rules.description: Client generated predominantly 4xx responses across the corpus or within a single day, consistent with path brute forcing or vulnerability scanning.
rules.falsePositives: Broken-link crawlers, misconfigured monitoring, uptime checks against a removed path.

rules.name: Sensitive file or backup probing
rules.description: Request for a well-known sensitive file (.env, wp-config, .git, phpinfo, web.config, debug consoles) or a backup/editor artefact extension that returned 404. Escalates to medium per IP at the threshold.
rules.falsePositives: Developers fetching their own configuration from internal hosts.

rules.name: Scanner or tooling user agent
rules.description: User agent matches a known scanner, exploitation framework or scripting library, or is empty from a public address.
rules.falsePositives: Authorized vulnerability scans, health checks, partner integrations using HTTP libraries.

rules.name: Invalid HTTP method or 405/501
rules.description: Request used a method outside the valid HTTP/WebDAV set, or the server answered 405/501. Garbage methods are typical of protocol fuzzers and scanners.
rules.falsePositives: WebDAV clients against sites without WebDAV.

rules.name: IIS request filtering block
rules.description: Request was rejected by IIS request filtering (404.7 extension, 404.8 hidden segment, 404.11 double escape, etc.). Escalates to medium per IP at the threshold.
rules.falsePositives: Legitimate users with very long query strings (404.15).

rules.name: Directory listing or handler denial
rules.description: 403.14/403.18/403.19/403.502/403.503: attempts to list directories or execute in disallowed pools, or blocked by dynamic IP restriction.
rules.falsePositives: Users browsing to a folder URL without a default document.

rules.name: Rapid path enumeration
rules.description: Client requested many distinct paths within a short tumbling window.
rules.falsePositives: Single-page applications loading many resources on first visit (usually internal).

rules.name: PHP/Xdebug information probe
rules.description: Query string requests phpinfo / xdebug information from a public address.
rules.falsePositives: None expected on a .NET server.

rules.name: Generic mass-scanner profile (PHP probes on .NET server)
rules.description: Public client requested only PHP/CGI/Perl paths and never a .NET handler, typical of untargeted internet scanning.
rules.falsePositives: None; informational for noise reduction.

rules.name: PHP-CGI argument injection (CVE-2024-4577 / CVE-2012-1823)
rules.description: Query contains soft-hyphen or dash '-d' PHP ini overrides such as allow_url_include / auto_prepend_file=php://input. Severity follows the response (gradeByStatus): as listed when the server answered 2xx or 5xx, one level lower for 3xx, low for 4xx and other failed requests.
rules.falsePositives: None realistic.

rules.name: Path traversal
rules.description: Dot-dot sequences or their encoded forms in the stem or query. Severity follows the response (gradeByStatus): as listed when the server answered 2xx or 5xx, one level lower for 3xx, low for 4xx and other failed requests.
rules.falsePositives: Rare: applications passing relative paths in parameters.

rules.name: SQL injection tokens
rules.description: Decoded query contains high-confidence SQL injection tokens (UNION SELECT, WAITFOR DELAY, xp_cmdshell, information_schema) or two or more medium-confidence tokens. Severity follows the response (gradeByStatus): as listed when the server answered 2xx or 5xx, one level lower for 3xx, low for 4xx and other failed requests.
rules.falsePositives: Search pages where users type SQL-like text; reporting tools passing SQL fragments.

rules.name: Command or code injection tokens
rules.description: Stem or decoded query contains shell commands, PowerShell, certutil, JNDI lookups, script tags or command chaining. Severity follows the response (gradeByStatus): as listed when the server answered 2xx or 5xx, one level lower for 3xx, low for 4xx and other failed requests.
rules.falsePositives: Help-desk or ticketing systems where users paste commands.

rules.name: .NET / IIS specific probing
rules.description: .NET Remoting endpoints (*.rem, *.soap), Telerik RAU, ELMAH/trace.axd, WebResource/ScriptResource padding-oracle (500 with d=), and ?wsdl/?disco on *.asmx/*.svc returning 500. Severity follows the response (gradeByStatus): as listed when the server answered 2xx or 5xx, one level lower for 3xx, low for 4xx and other failed requests.
rules.falsePositives: Legitimate SOAP clients fetching WSDL (status 200 is not flagged).

rules.name: Known product exploit path
rules.description: Request for a path associated with exploitation of a specific product (Exchange, SharePoint, Citrix, Fortinet, Struts, Spring, Confluence, Ivanti, F5...). Escalates to high when any hit returned 200 or 500.
rules.falsePositives: The product actually runs on this server.

rules.name: Server error following exploit attempt
rules.description: Status 500 for the same client and path within the window after an exploitation-rule hit from that client.
rules.falsePositives: Fragile applications that error on any malformed input.

rules.name: Oversized or high-entropy request
rules.description: Very long stem or query, or a long high-entropy query typical of serialized payloads.
rules.falsePositives: Applications passing encrypted tokens or state in GET parameters.

rules.name: Malformed / aborted request from public client
rules.description: 400/413/414/431 from a public client, or an aborted connection on a POST to an executable handler.
rules.falsePositives: Mobile clients on poor networks.

rules.name: New executable path reached from the internet
rules.description: An executable-extension path first appeared after the baseline period, was requested by a public client and returned 200. Classic indicator of a newly planted web shell. Paths requested by many distinct addresses are treated as application releases and excluded.
rules.falsePositives: New application pages deployed after the baseline; review first-seen date against change records.

rules.name: Executable in upload or static directory
rules.description: An executable-extension path under an upload/attachment/static directory returned 200.
rules.falsePositives: Applications that legitimately host handlers in such folders (e.g. an UploadAttachment.aspx page).

rules.name: Interactive web shell fingerprint
rules.description: Executable path used only by one or two public clients, mostly with POST and mostly 200.
rules.falsePositives: Single remote user of a niche page; API integrations from a partner.

rules.name: Web shell names, parameters or client user agents
rules.description: Basename matches common web shell names, query contains shell parameters (cmd=, z0=, action=cmd...), or the user agent matches AntSword/Godzilla/Behinder/Weevely. Severity follows the response (gradeByStatus): as listed when the server answered 2xx or 5xx, one level lower for 3xx, low for 4xx and other failed requests.
rules.falsePositives: Pages named cmd.aspx or test.aspx in legacy applications.

rules.name: Static extension handled like a script
rules.description: POST, or GET with a non-versioning query, to an image/text/config extension returned 200 to a public client (handler mapping abuse, polyglot shells).
rules.falsePositives: Image resizing handlers; analytics beacons on .gif.

rules.name: Automation profile: only executable handlers, no static assets
rules.description: Public client whose requests are almost entirely executable handlers with zero static assets, and which mostly succeeds (at least 5 2xx, at most half 4xx): a script or tool driving the application rather than a browser or a 404-heavy scanner.
rules.falsePositives: Mobile apps and SOAP/API integrations calling .asmx/.ashx endpoints.

rules.name: Exploit then new executable path from same client
rules.description: The first client to request an executable path (with 200) had triggered an exploitation rule before the path first appeared.
rules.falsePositives: Scanners that later browse normal pages.

rules.name: Login endpoint brute force
rules.description: Many POST requests to login endpoints from one client within a tumbling window.
rules.falsePositives: Shared NAT egress of many users; load tests.

rules.name: Repeated 401 responses
rules.description: Many 401 responses for one client within a tumbling window; escalated to high when a 200/302 followed within 5 minutes.
rules.falsePositives: Windows Integrated Authentication negotiation produces 401 pairs; review counts.

rules.name: Authenticated account activity of interest
rules.description: cs-username populated and either seen for the first time, used from a public address, or a privileged/generic account name.
rules.falsePositives: Expected service accounts.

rules.name: Internal off-hours use of application handlers
rules.description: Internal client made many executable-handler requests outside configured business hours on a given day (excluding the learned scheduler heartbeat).
rules.falsePositives: Night shifts, batch jobs, polling dashboards left open.

rules.name: User-agent rotation
rules.description: Public client used many distinct user agents within one day, typical of credential-stuffing or scanner tooling.
rules.falsePositives: Carrier-grade NAT and corporate proxies.

rules.name: Outdated browser user agent reaching executable handlers
rules.description: A browser user agent whose version was at least minAgeDays old when it was first seen (or a browser past its end of support, such as Internet Explorer), used by no more than maxIps clients, received 2xx responses from executable handlers for public clients. Attack tools and scripts often hard-code an old browser string. Release dates come from lists\browser-releases.txt.
rules.falsePositives: Unmanaged or embedded clients (kiosks, scanners, line-of-business applications) that are never updated; check the clients and their behaviour.

rules.name: Spoofed, malformed or automation user agent
rules.description: User agent used by public clients that cannot exist (browser version not released yet, not available for the stated Windows version, or a Windows version that does not exist), is malformed, or names a headless browser or automation tool. Escalates to medium when public clients received 2xx responses from executable handlers with it.
rules.falsePositives: Privacy tools and extensions that randomise the user agent; monitoring that uses headless browsers; home-grown clients with a hand-written user agent.

rules.name: Exploit payload in the user agent
rules.description: The user agent carries an exploit payload: Log4Shell lookups (${jndi:...}), Shellshock (() { :; };), OGNL, script tags, SQL or shell injection. The response status says little here: such payloads target logging and back-end components and often act out of band.
rules.falsePositives: Security scanners run by the organisation.

rules.name: Archive / database / document downloaded by public client
rules.description: Public client received 200 for an archive, backup, database, mailbox, office or config file outside public download directories. High for .bak/.mdf/.sql/.config/.pst-class extensions.
rules.falsePositives: Public document libraries; add them to lists/public-download-directories.txt.

rules.name: Large or long-running response to public client
rules.description: 200 response with sc-bytes above the threshold (if logged) or time-taken above the threshold.
rules.falsePositives: Slow mobile clients; long-polling endpoints.

rules.name: Download / attachment / export endpoint use by public client
rules.description: Public client hit a download/attachment/export/report endpoint. Escalates to medium per IP when the hourly rate reaches the threshold.
rules.falsePositives: Remote staff using the ERP from home.

rules.name: Document ID enumeration
rules.description: Many distinct query strings against a single download/attachment endpoint from one client within an hour.
rules.falsePositives: Bulk export jobs.

rules.name: Logging gap
rules.description: Missing daily log files inside the corpus span, or no rows for at least the threshold while surrounding traffic is continuous.
rules.falsePositives: Server shutdowns, maintenance, sites with no overnight traffic.

rules.name: Worker process restarts
rules.description: File contains many more header blocks than is normal for this corpus (each block marks a worker process or logging restart; threshold = max(blocksPerFile, medianFactor x median blocks per file)), or a restart coincides with HTTP 500 errors (escalated to medium).
rules.falsePositives: Scheduled application pool recycling (every 1740 minutes by default), deployments.

rules.name: Timestamp anomalies
rules.description: Timestamps go backwards inside a header block, or file content dates disagree with the filename date beyond the rollover tolerance.
rules.falsePositives: Clock corrections (NTP) produce small backwards steps.

rules.name: Undersized or truncated log file
rules.description: File is much smaller than the median of the same weekday in surrounding weeks, or ends without a newline.
rules.falsePositives: Holidays; the final file of a collection is normally partial.

rules.name: Logging configuration change
rules.description: #Fields schema or #Software version changed mid-corpus.
rules.falsePositives: IIS upgrades, administrator adding fields.

rules.name: Heartbeat absent
rules.description: Loopback scheduler traffic normally present every hour stopped for two or more hours on a day where it otherwise ran.
rules.falsePositives: Application pool stopped for maintenance.

rules.name: Malformed or undecodable content
rules.description: Malformed rows, non-ASCII bytes or URL decode errors exceed the threshold share of a file.
rules.falsePositives: Non-UTF-8 logging with localized content.

rules.name: Example custom rule: POST to /webcrm from public client
rules.description: Template showing the custom rule format. Enable or copy to create your own.
